top.title: Tinubu doing fantastic job on sports infrastructure, says Infantino
top.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has commended President Bola Tinubu’s administration for its investment in sports infrastructure, describing its efforts as a “fantastic job” and an indication of Nigeria’s commitment to the future of its young population. Infantino gave the commendation on Saturday while addressing the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) in Abuja. The FIFA president urged members of the Nigerian delegation to convey his regards to Tinubu, while acknowledging the contributions of the President and other Nigerian leaders to sports development. “On behalf of President Tinubu, please send him our warmest regards. He is doing together with all of you. Fantastic job here in Nigeria, showing that you are a country projected into the future,” Infantino said. He particularly praised investments in sports facilities, noting that they reflected confidence in the potential of young Nigerians. “We were discussing this yesterday as well, also with the Chairman of the National Sports Commission, my brother Shehu. The investments done in sports facilities infrastructure show that you believe in your youth, in the young girls and the young boys of Nigeria,” he said. “Thank you for that. Congratulations for that,” he added. Infantino also thanked Nigeria for hosting him and his delegation, which included FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström, describing the visit as an opportunity to reconnect with the continent. “Thanks for welcoming me and our delegation with the Secretary-General and the others here at home in Africa, in Abuja. Thank you for your support. It means the world to me,” he said. His remarks followed an inspection of sports infrastructure projects in Nigeria on Friday, including the remodelled Warri City Stadium and the Hussey College mini-stadium and sports complex in Delta State. He also visited the ongoing FIFA Forward Technical Centre project at the Moshood Abiola National Stadium in Abuja, describing the facility as an investment in the future of Nigerian football. “This is a collaboration between Nigerian football and FIFA for the future of the girls and the boys of Nigeria,” he said. During his visit to the Warri City Stadium, Infantino stressed the importance of developing grassroots sports facilities to ensure that football remained accessible to people across communities. “That’s what football is about. It’s for everyone, everywhere. It’s the big stadiums, it’s the World Cup, but it’s also the smaller stadiums, it’s the proximity,” he said. The FIFA president also expressed appreciation for the reception he received in Nigeria, assuring the country of the world football governing body’s continued support. “I feel so much the love of Africa, the love of Nigeria. I am very happy to be here. You can always count on FIFA. We are not just your partners; we are your family members,” he added. Infantino’s visit also coincided with Nigeria’s endorsement of his bid for another term as FIFA

top.title: Odukoya drags sister, others to court over removal as senior pastor
top.description: The Senior Pastor of the Fountain of Life Church, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, has dragged his sister and others before a Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his purported removal from office and the decisions taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees. Odukoya, alongside the Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church, instituted the action against eight defendants, including Pastor Tolu Odukoya, Mr Biodun Balogun, Mr Biodun Awosika, Pastor Rotimi Okpaise, Pastor Tobi Enuha, Pastor Gbenga Onabanjo, Pastor Fred Ohiani and Pastor Akin Osinbajo. This is coming some days after a Lagos State High Court had restrained him from parading as the senior pastor in the church. Odukoya in an affidavit in support of the applications is asking the court to determine whether meetings held by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the decisions taken at those meetings complied with the church’s constitution. Odukoya said he was appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees at an emergency meeting of the board on September 14, 2023, and was subsequently installed in September of the same year. He said the church and its organs were governed by its constitution, amended by a special resolution dated January 16, 2003, and that the defendants were members of its Board of Trustees. According to his affidavit, the disagreement began after a December 19, 2025, meeting of the board, attended by Bishop Mike Okonkwo, at which the possibility of handing over the church’s administrative arm to the Associate Senior Pastor was discussed. He said no resolution or final decision was reached at the meeting. Board meeting Odukoya said he subsequently convened a board meeting for January 5, 2026, but it could not hold because there was no quorum. He added that some trustees later presented proposals to him, many of which he declined because, according to him, they were inconsistent with the church’s constitution. He said the trustees subsequently sent him a letter dated January 7, 2026, requesting a response within three days, but he did not see it until after the deadline had elapsed. Odukoya said he later directed the board secretary to schedule a meeting for January 30, 2026, after a request for a special meeting was made by a board member. However, he alleged that a separate notice for a meeting on January 22 was circulated by the fourth defendant and did not come from the board secretariat. “I received the notice late in the evening of January 20, 2026, effectively giving me one day notice of the purported meeting,” he stated. He said he declined to attend the meeting, but the defendants proceeded with it under the name of “concerned members of the Board”. top.title: Rapid Reaction: Northwestern falls 20-17 in heartbreaker to Minnesota
top.description: Nov 21, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Northwestern Wildcats quarterback Nicco Marchiol (4) celebrates his touchdown against the Minnesota Golden Gophers during the second half at Huntington Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Northwestern loses in heartbreaking fashion as it falls to Minnesota 20-17. In a game that looked poised to go to overtime after the ‘Cats scored with just 27 seconds remaining in the game, Minnesota gave payback for last year’s Wrigley Field matchup by kicking a walk-off field goal to win the game. Nicco Marchiol had a solid day and performed well in the eye test, but there were a plethora of incompletions that could have altered the result of the game. He completed 13-of-23 passing attempts for 169 yards and a touchdown. For the first time in quite a while, Northwestern found some room in the run game with running back Caleb Komolafe rushing 19 times for 109 yards. Griffin Wilde also had a solid game, catching five passes for 77 yards and a touchdown. Luke Dehnicke showed his emerging talent as a tight end, catching three passes for 66 yards. This game marks the first four-game losing streak in the David Braun era at Northwestern. The Gophers kicked it away for a touchback to open the penultimate regular-season game. The ‘Cats’ offense started things off with runs to Komolafe and Drew Wagner, picking up the first down to move the chains. Komolafe then broke off a 14-yard run to keep things going, but Minnesota’s defense forced an incompletion and short run to bring up third down. Another Marchiol incompletion to Wilde brought out Northwestern’s punt unit, and the Gophers’ first possession started at their own 20. Minnesota QB Drake Lindsey started out in the air with completions to his tight end Roman Voss and running back Darius Taylor to bring up a third-and-4. The ‘Cats stood strong, and Jamaal Johnson got home for a sack to force the punt. The three-and-out gave NU the ball right back at the 43-yard line. On offense, a second-down jet sweep to Drew Wagner squeaked the ‘Cats past the first-down marker, but then Marchiol and Wilde failed to connect yet again to put NU behind schedule. A fake handoff led to Marchiol being drilled behind the line of scrimmage, setting up a third-and-15 where Sawchuk’s run barely got back to the initial line of scrimmage. Minnesota’s game plan stayed the same on its second drive, opening with a short pass to Jalen Smith and a short run by Darius Taylor to pick up a first down. After two short gains, Northwestern surged into the backfield on third-and-short, but Minnesota’s TJ Thomas’ second effort kept the drive alive. Thomas then picked up 18 yards on a short completion as the Gopher offense found a rhythm and moved to the Northwestern 42. However, a holding call a couple of plays later led to Minnesota stalling out and setting up a 48-yard field goal try. The Gophers’ kicker pulled the ball left, and the game remained scoreless.

top.title: Ravens’ 2026 season has come to a crashing halt
top.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Trainers attend to Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens kneels after getting hurt on the first play of the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images It took just one play. As optimistically as it began, the 2026 Ravens season is all but finished. On the first day of November, on his first snap back from a high-ankle sprain, Lamar Jackson injured his right thumb when his throwing hand struck the wrist of Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau. Jackson knew something was wrong immediately, sprinting straight to the sideline and then to the locker room. The two-time MVP has since had surgery on his thumb with a late-season return technically in play – if it even matters. At this point, Jackson is the Baltimore Ravens, and his contract reflects that. Many want to bash the supporting cast, the coaches and the front office, but it just isn’t realistic for a team paying a star quarterback that much to also have stars at every other position. What did the Chiefs look like without Patrick Mahomes last year? What did the Bengals look like without Joe Burrow? What would the Bills look like without Josh Allen? On top of losing Jackson, the Ravens have suffered a rash of injuries elsewhere, primarily on the offensive line. A position group that typically thrives on continuity is operating with a new offensive coordinator, a new offensive line coach, and a rotating door of new starters. This year, the unit has had five different centers and four different right guards. Has the offensive line been good enough? No. But we never got to see the vision. Heck, we never even got to see Jackson and Zay Flowers play a full game together. The full extent of the Ravens’ woes came to a head five days after the Jacksonville Jaguars. With undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano making his first start, the Ravens were once again trounced at home, this time in a downpour. We all expected the offense to struggle, and predictably, it did. But once again, the defense let the dam break. Is that partly a product of the offense’s struggles? Probably. Still, it looked more like a group of unmotivated, aging players struggling to adjust to a new defensive system. Marlon Humphrey and Malaki Starks were both burned for big plays, and the middle of the field — an area that has plagued this defense for years — was wide open all night for Trevor Lawrence. And yet, Monday night’s loss to the Chargers might have been worse. Jacoby Brissett performed admirable in his Ravens debut, but an anemic running game and a defense that once again could not tackle gifted a winless team their first victory. Unfortunately, the near future doesn’t look much brighter, largely because of some questionable decisions by the front office. top.title: Browns Get Credit for Contract Move on $13 Million Newcomer
top.description: Quincy Williams #5 of the Cleveland Browns Getty Most of the offseason for the Cleveland Browns was focused first on the overhaul of the offensive line in March, followed by another big NFL draft haul in April, one which was widely predicted to be successful (and has probably even exceeded those expectations). But tucked in among those move was an underrated one: the Browns brought in a favorite of new defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg by signing former Jets linebacker Quincy Williams, whose style of play on the field is as dynamic as his mouth can be during interviews. Rutenberg was Williams’ position coach with the Jets, and Williams was an All-Pro in 2023 under Rutenberg’s watch. After signing a two-year, $13 million contract ($17 million with incentives), Williams said, “Not to be cocky, but the first thing (Retunberg) did was come and get me.” The move has worked. The Browns lost productive linebacker Devin Bush after last season, and needed a new running mate for star Carson Schwesinger. So far, Williams has fit the bill. He is rated the No. 7 linebacker in the league at Pro Football Focus, out of 82 in total. Quincy Williams a Success for the Browns At ESPN, the Browns’ signing of Williams–which has been largely overlooked–got some praise in an article by Aaron Schatz. Browns LB Quincy Williams: “They be barking. We be biting.” pic.twitter.com/kTXVyxOYWG — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) October 2, 2026 He writes : “Quincy Williams had only 12 starts for the Jets last season and turned 30 in August, so it was reasonable to assume that he was at the tail end of his career. The Browns brought him in on a reasonable contract and stuck him next to Defensive Rookie of the Year Carson Schwesinger , and Williams has been an outstanding playmaker in that role. … “Williams is known for speed and has been excellent in pass coverage, with four passes defensed and 15 pass tackles, which prevented a successful yardage gain despite a reception. Opposing running backs have fewer than 20 receiving yards per game against the Browns.” Two of Williams’ biggest incentives are still possible, but they are longshots –$500,000 for four sacks, and $500,000 for three interceptions. That would double if the Browns make the playoffs, which they are in good position to do. top.description: Nov 21, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) drives for a shot against Milwaukee Bucks center Myles Turner (3) during the second quarter at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Joel Embiid’s 26-point, 17-rebound effort was enough to push the Sixers past Tyler Herro’s 50-point night, with Philadelphia escaping 132-129 after Herro’s last-second three was ruled out. LeBron James added 21-6-6 to guide the 76ers to the win. Here’s what I saw. Just good enough to win This was a classic edition of a 1 pm game against a nonsense team for the Sixers. The first 24 minutes featured pretty miserable defense, no attention to detail on the glass, and some funky lineups for Philadelphia. But they had beautiful passing in half-court offense and ran the floor well, so they emerged with a one-point lead at halftime while exerting close to minimal effort. This was not the usual Embiid sautee of Myles Turner, who did a good job of bothering his shots and minimizing foul trouble in the first half. But Embiid’s shot was the only thing missing from an otherwise complete half, as he spent most of it playmaking out of the high post as the Bucks let cutters waltz down the middle of the lane. Embiid dropped dimes to LeBron James, VJ Edgecombe, and Jabari Walker as Milwaukee shaded help in his direction, with the Sixers doing a good job of sprinting through the middle every time the seas parted. top.title: Davies explains Birmingham star’s absence against Stoke – and reacts to defeat

George Hirst scored the only goal shortly after half-time to knock Blues off the top of the Championship, despite Birmingham playing against ten men for the final half an hour after Luca Bombino was sent off. “We needed to do more,” Davies said on his side’s performance after the red card. “I expected us to do more than we did with that amount of time. Creativity is a good word to highlight. “Sometimes it’s about getting crosses in, causing that little bit of chaos, seeing if we can get a second ball, and not trying to score the perfect goal basically. “Then you go to the quality of the crossing, arriving in the right positions, and it was all just off the level it needed to be. “You always have to give credit when the opposition holds on and does it doggedly like Stoke did. Fair play to them for that but we expect more from ourselves.” Davies also provided an update on Jhon Solis, who missed the game after picking up a knock while on international duty. “Jhon picked up a knock on international duty that we thought he would run off,” he said. “But he wasn’t able to do that. “My understanding is that it’s not a long-term thing but it was investigated more today so we should know tomorrow.” Asked whether Solis could be available on Wednesday, Davies added: “I think there is a chance but I don’t know how big that chance is right now based on what I was told yesterday.”

top.description: Heavy rain led to poor course conditions at Sea Island Resort's Seaside Course in St. Simon's Island, Georgia, forcing the PGA Tour to postpone Saturday's third round of the 2026 RSM Classic to Sunday and push the final round back to Monday. So what about fans who had tickets to see Saturday's action in-person? Tough luck. The RSM Classic put out a statement on social media Saturday afternoon noting that only fans with tickets for Sunday would be allowed in the gates for the third round. "Only Sunday tickets will be accepted tomorrow," the tournament wrote in an Instagram post . "Due to our refund and exchange policy, we will not honor Saturday tickets tomorrow." The tournament also said no spectators will be in attendance for Monday's final round, meaning the last 18 holes of the PGA Tour's 2026 season will be played without a gallery. "Grounds will be closed to all patrons on Monday," the post's caption read. "Golf Channel will televise the event so watch there." There's a three-way tie atop the leaderboard after 36 holes between Michael Thorbjornsen, Marco Penge and Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen, and there are another 13 players within two shots of the lead. It's also crunch time for several players who are fighting to get inside the top 100 in the FedEx Cup standings, the threshold required to keep a PGA Tour card for the 2027 season. top.title: Grading Purdue football: Questionable QB decision and Fs all-around in blowout loss to Wisconsin
top.description: WEST LAFAYETTE − Purdue football 's nose dive continues. The Boilermakers had the ball just 49 seconds before they trailed 14-0. Wisconsin (7-4) had the opening it needed on its way to a 42-10 victory . The Badgers sent Purdue (3-8) fans exiting the season's final home game with a fifth straight loss, and now with 19 consecutive losses in the series. A questionable starting quarterback decision backfired and Purdue's wet paper bag defense again provided a big day for a struggling offense. In a season marred by failures, you can imagine how the report card looks from Purdue's loss to Wisconsin at Ross-Ade Stadium. OFFENSE GRADE: F The offensive line was supposed to be an upgrade this year, but it's becoming hard to find evidence supporting that claim. Not a lot of analysis needs to go into this grade. Statistics are all you need. Purdue averaged 3.6 yards per play and totaled 199 yards. DEFENSE GRADE: F By halftime, the Badgers already had accumulated 52 more rushing yards (185) than their season average (133). Purdue's defense is beyond repair. Wisconsin quarterback Colton Joseph didn't start the last two games but returned behind center after Ryan Hopkins was injured late in a Nov. 14 game against Maryland. Joseph then became the latest QB to torch the Big Ten's worst defense. The Badgers totaled 508 yards, 381 of those on the ground. Wisconsin was 13-for-17 on converting third and fourth downs. SPECIAL TEAMS GRADE: B Jacobo Echeverria Lozano attempted, and made, a career-long 53-yard field goal in the second quarter. It pads his case for the Lou Groza Award, which is bolstered because Purdue's offense is good, but not good enough to get into the end zone in a lot of cases. Still, the freshman has taken advantage. Dylan Drennan also has been a weapon, though Purdue doesn't have a competent enough defense to fully benefit from Drennan's leg. The risk returning kickoffs has not paid off. Best bet for Purdue is to take the touchback, or fair catch if the kickoff doesn't reach the end zone. COACHING GRADE: F You can't give me a valid reason why quarterback Evans Chuba started this game over Ryan Browne. No package or perceived advantage makes sense. It's even more indefensible after seeing the results of that decision. Chuba threw two incompletions during a three-and-out. Browne led Purdue on consecutive scoring drives after entering. Purdue had a second week to tinker with the defense since Kevin Kane's firing , and somehow looked better on the road against a ranked Iowa team with little time to adapt to the staff change. Waiting until you're down 18 points to uncover the trick play portion of the playbook seems like off timing. GAME MVP If Ryan Hopkins is healthy, Colton Joseph probably doesn't even start this game. Instead, Joseph's return as the Badgers starting quarterback. He rushed for 187 yards and 2 touchdowns, passed for 114 yards and also hauled in a 13-yard touchdown reception. top.title: MLS star Thomas Muller explains how promotion and relegation changes league dynamic
top.description: MLS star Thomas Muller explains how promotion and relegation changes league dynamic originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Now 37 years old, Thomas Muller has greatly enjoyed his time in Major League Soccer. After leaving Bayern Munich in the summer of 2025 following a glittering 17-year career with the Bavarian giants, Muller joined the Vancouver Whitecaps and has brought his winning mentality along. Muller reached the MLS Cup final in his first half-season, losing to Lionel Messi and Inter Miami at the final hurdle. This season, Vancouver won the Western Conference regular season title, and are set to be the No. 1 seed on their side of the bracket in the playoffs. Always his enlightening, outspoken self, Muller took the time to explain how MLS is different without promotion and relegation, from a player's perspective. He believes there are real, on-field consequences to having a closed pyramid, ones which players can notice by the style of play across the league. MORE: Explaining the Jamal Musiala contract dispute which has Bayern Munich receiving criticism Thomas Muller explains how MLS is different without relegation Thomas Muller was asked how he feels Major League Soccer handles being a closed, single-entity league without promotion and relegation. The 37-year-old stopped short of criticizing the league for not having promotion and relegation, but he did explain the differences between having open movement throughout the pyramid and having a closed system without the threat of relegation at the bottom of the table. As Muller explains, there is a pressure for those under relegation threat that changes the way some teams play. Without that threat, as there is in MLS, teams play more openly — more risky, as Muller insinuates — which can increase the range of possible performances. It can cause players to make excellent plays, but also commit grave errors you wouldn't see in a less-risky playing style at a team battling relegation. "There is no relegation," Muller explained at the end of the 2026 regular season. "There is no big pressure. There is 'oh yea, we do a rebuild.' Nobody's happy to lose, but it's totally different when you fight for getting relegated. Maybe you lose, but for the whole year, the whole club, you lose people working at the club and the budget changes. It's totally different for fans, the pressure. The players maybe have no contract for next year when you go down. "So the playing style changes. When you play a bottom-of-the-league team in Europe, they fight for their lives. nigeria.title: Tinubu doing fantastic job on sports infrastructure, says Infantino
nigeria.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has commended President Bola Tinubu’s administration for its investment in sports infrastructure, describing its efforts as a “fantastic job” and an indication of Nigeria’s commitment to the future of its young population. Infantino gave the commendation on Saturday while addressing the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) in Abuja. The FIFA president urged members of the Nigerian delegation to convey his regards to Tinubu, while acknowledging the contributions of the President and other Nigerian leaders to sports development. “On behalf of President Tinubu, please send him our warmest regards. He is doing together with all of you. Fantastic job here in Nigeria, showing that you are a country projected into the future,” Infantino said. He particularly praised investments in sports facilities, noting that they reflected confidence in the potential of young Nigerians. “We were discussing this yesterday as well, also with the Chairman of the National Sports Commission, my brother Shehu. The investments done in sports facilities infrastructure show that you believe in your youth, in the young girls and the young boys of Nigeria,” he said. “Thank you for that. Congratulations for that,” he added. Infantino also thanked Nigeria for hosting him and his delegation, which included FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström, describing the visit as an opportunity to reconnect with the continent. “Thanks for welcoming me and our delegation with the Secretary-General and the others here at home in Africa, in Abuja. Thank you for your support. It means the world to me,” he said. His remarks followed an inspection of sports infrastructure projects in Nigeria on Friday, including the remodelled Warri City Stadium and the Hussey College mini-stadium and sports complex in Delta State. He also visited the ongoing FIFA Forward Technical Centre project at the Moshood Abiola National Stadium in Abuja, describing the facility as an investment in the future of Nigerian football. “This is a collaboration between Nigerian football and FIFA for the future of the girls and the boys of Nigeria,” he said. During his visit to the Warri City Stadium, Infantino stressed the importance of developing grassroots sports facilities to ensure that football remained accessible to people across communities. “That’s what football is about. It’s for everyone, everywhere. It’s the big stadiums, it’s the World Cup, but it’s also the smaller stadiums, it’s the proximity,” he said. The FIFA president also expressed appreciation for the reception he received in Nigeria, assuring the country of the world football governing body’s continued support. “I feel so much the love of Africa, the love of Nigeria. I am very happy to be here. You can always count on FIFA. We are not just your partners; we are your family members,” he added. Infantino’s visit also coincided with Nigeria’s endorsement of his bid for another term as FIFA

nigeria.title: Odukoya drags sister, others to court over removal as senior pastor
nigeria.description: The Senior Pastor of the Fountain of Life Church, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, has dragged his sister and others before a Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his purported removal from office and the decisions taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees. Odukoya, alongside the Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church, instituted the action against eight defendants, including Pastor Tolu Odukoya, Mr Biodun Balogun, Mr Biodun Awosika, Pastor Rotimi Okpaise, Pastor Tobi Enuha, Pastor Gbenga Onabanjo, Pastor Fred Ohiani and Pastor Akin Osinbajo. This is coming some days after a Lagos State High Court had restrained him from parading as the senior pastor in the church. Odukoya in an affidavit in support of the applications is asking the court to determine whether meetings held by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the decisions taken at those meetings complied with the church’s constitution. Odukoya said he was appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees at an emergency meeting of the board on September 14, 2023, and was subsequently installed in September of the same year. He said the church and its organs were governed by its constitution, amended by a special resolution dated January 16, 2003, and that the defendants were members of its Board of Trustees. According to his affidavit, the disagreement began after a December 19, 2025, meeting of the board, attended by Bishop Mike Okonkwo, at which the possibility of handing over the church’s administrative arm to the Associate Senior Pastor was discussed. He said no resolution or final decision was reached at the meeting. Board meeting Odukoya said he subsequently convened a board meeting for January 5, 2026, but it could not hold because there was no quorum. He added that some trustees later presented proposals to him, many of which he declined because, according to him, they were inconsistent with the church’s constitution. He said the trustees subsequently sent him a letter dated January 7, 2026, requesting a response within three days, but he did not see it until after the deadline had elapsed. Odukoya said he later directed the board secretary to schedule a meeting for January 30, 2026, after a request for a special meeting was made by a board member. However, he alleged that a separate notice for a meeting on January 22 was circulated by the fourth defendant and did not come from the board secretariat. “I received the notice late in the evening of January 20, 2026, effectively giving me one day notice of the purported meeting,” he stated. He said he declined to attend the meeting, but the defendants proceeded with it under the name of “concerned members of the Board”. nigeria.title: Arsenal held by Newcastle rally and lose Raya to injury
nigeria.description: Arsenal missed the chance to open up an eight-point lead at the top of the Premier League after a stirring second-half fightback from Newcastle held the defending champions to a 2-2 draw on Saturday. The Gunners led through Eberechi Eze’s strike after a dominant first 45 minutes. But Mikel Arteta’s men were suddenly headed for defeat when goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw provided a much-needed boost for under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle. Noni Madueke salvaged a point for Arsenal and stretched their lead at the top over surprise package Brighton to six points. However, the loss of influential goalkeeper David Raya to injury could provide a twist in the title race that many believed Arsenal would cruise. Newcastle remain in the bottom half of the table with just one win in six games in all competitions. Yet, Jaissle can point to his side’s second half performance as a potential turning point after a difficult start to his reign at St. James’ Park. Arsenal move back six points clear of third-placed Manchester City, but missed the chance to put their foot down in the defence of their title. Madueke continued his impressive form in the injury absence of Bukayo Saka and hit the post early on. Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes was roundly booed on his first return to Tyneside since making a £75 million ($98 million) move to the Emirates Stadium In August. The Brazilian nearly silenced his former faithful when he prodded just wide from a Madueke cross as Arsenal pressed for the opener. It duly arrived 10 minutes before the break when Kai Havertz pounced on a poor touch by Lewis Hall and brilliantly played in Eze to blast high past Lukas Hornicek. Jaissle got the response he needed from his half-time team talk as Newcastle came out a completely different proposition after the break. Arsenal also played a part in letting the home side back into the game and lifting the 50,000 crowd in doing so. Martin Odegaard shanked his attempt at a long ball forward to allow William Osula to play in Barnes to level. Suddenly an Arsenal side that had kept seven clean sheets in their opening 10 league games was on the rocks. Thiaw bundled home a second for Newcastle just 13 minutes later after Dan Burn was left completely unmarked from a corner and his header was only parried by Raya. That proved to be one of Raya’s final interventions as the Spaniard had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga. Raya would be a massive miss if the Spaniard is sidelined for a significant spell. nigeria.title: 2027 Election: INEC failed on voters’ register – ADC
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has described the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC’s decision to postpone the clean-up of the national voters’ register until after the 2027 general elections as a major failure. The party said INEC had four years to prepare for the exercise. However, ADC said the voters’ register is only one of several issues that will determine the credibility of the 2027 elections. They pointed to electronic transmission of results, result collation and compliance with the Electoral Act as other major areas of concern. Speaking to Vanguard, the ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, said INEC’s failure to clean up the register raised questions about its commitment to conducting credible elections. “This shouldn’t have happened. INEC had four years to prepare and plan for this, and its failure to do so does not suggest that it is taking its responsibilities seriously, particularly the issue of maintaining a credible voters’ register,” he said. Abdullahi, however, said the party would not make the outcome of the 2027 elections depend solely on whether INEC produced a credible voters’ register, noting that previous elections had been conducted despite imperfections in the register. “We do not believe that the credibility of the 2027 general election rests solely on INEC’s ability to produce a credible voters’ register. It would have given everyone greater confidence if the commission had been able to do so, but we are not going to hinge the fate of the 2027 election on that single issue.” He said the ADC was also concerned about how INEC would implement the Electoral Act, particularly the electronic transmission of results from polling units, the collation process and the duties of electoral officers regarding Forms EC8A and EC8E. “There are other, more pertinent issues of concern to our party. These include compliance with the Electoral Act, the electronic transmission of results from polling units, the collation of results and the additional responsibilities assigned to electoral officers regarding Forms EC8A and EC8E.” On the possible effect of the voters’ register on the elections, Abdullahi argued that strict compliance with the law, particularly provisions on voter accreditation, could reduce the impact of its shortcomings. “If INEC complies with the Electoral Act, particularly regarding voter accreditation, the shortcomings in the voters’ register may not have as much impact. Problems arise when the commission fails to abide by its own rules and the provisions of the Electoral Act,” he said. He said the ADC was studying possible weaknesses in the electoral process and making arrangements to ensure that its votes were protected. “We know where the loopholes are, and that is why we continue to focus on them and ensure that we make adequate arrangements to protect our votes.” Vanguard News The post 2027 Election: INEC failed on voters’ register – ADC appeared first

nigeria.title: ‘Duty of care’: Players’ union slams Bayern for Musiala comments
nigeria.description: Global players’ union FIFPRO has slammed Bayern Munich for putting pressure on midfielder Jamal Musiala to renegotiate his contract with the Bundesliga club as he recovers from injury. In a statement issued Saturday, the footballers’ union said recent public comments made by Bayern’s honorary president Uli Hoeness, current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen and former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge were part of a “coordinated campaign” to put pressure on Musiala. The Bayern bosses had questioned whether Musiala, who missed several matches with a neurological condition earlier in the season and has recently returned from a hamstring injury, should continue to receive his contracted salary. FIFPRO hit out at “a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations”. “A club of Bayern’s standing should know better,” the international union for professional football players said. “Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala… Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives. “Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.” The 23-year-old Germany international signed a contract extension in February 2025 until 2030 and is among Bayern’s top earners. Musiala missed six months after breaking his ankle at the Club World Cup in the summer of 2025. At the start of the 2026-27 season, Musiala collapsed twice on the pitch in pre-season. He later revealed he was suffering from a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”. Speaking Friday after Musiala came off the bench for his first Bayern appearance in two months, Rummenigge suggested the player would not be able to recapture his previous form. “Based on what we know, it unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he so often demonstrated here in this stadium,” Rummenigge said on Sky Germany. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable.” Bayern on Saturday announced record revenues of 988.2 million euros ($1.083 billion) for the 2025-26 season. nigeria.title: China Diaries: The Railway Connecting Continents
nigeria.description: Standing at the Xi’an International Port Station in northwest China, watching the movement of freight trains preparing to transport goods across borders and continents, I was reminded that economic development is not only about what a country produces. It is also about how efficiently it can move what it produces to the rest of the world. Xi’an occupies an interesting place in China’s history. It was once the starting point of the ancient Silk Road, which connected China to Central Asia, the Middle East and Europe through centuries of trade and cultural exchange. Today, the city is reclaiming that historic role through a modern railway network that connects Chinese manufacturing centres to markets across Europe and Asia. The China-Europe Railway Express is one of the most visible outcomes of China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). Through this network, freight trains transport automobiles, electronics, machinery, textiles, agricultural products and other goods across the Eurasian continent. What makes the initiative particularly interesting is how it has transformed the economic possibilities of a city located thousands of kilometres from the sea. Xi’an has become an important international logistics hub, demonstrating that geographical distance from a coastline does not have to limit a city’s participation in global trade. The railway network has continued to expand. By November 2025, China-Europe freight trains had completed nearly 120,000 journeys, connecting 232 cities in 26 European countries and more than 100 cities in 11 Asian countries. The value of goods transported through the network had reached $426.4 billion by the end of 2024. These are not merely impressive transportation figures. They represent an evolving system of economic connectivity, linking manufacturers, suppliers, distributors and consumers across national borders. Beyond transportation: The economics of connectivity The significance of the railway goes beyond moving containers from one destination to another. It creates opportunities for businesses to reach markets faster, diversify their supply chains and reduce their dependence on a single transportation route. nigeria.title: English village votes to ‘leave UK’ over migrant camp plan
nigeria.description: A small English village on Saturday voted to leave the UK in a symbolic poll protesting government plans to house hundreds of asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base. The vote in Barnham follows a similar protest referendum in the village of Piddington in September, also over government plans to move asylum seekers from hotels into former military accommodation. Between 400 to 500 people were eligible to vote in the ballot which carried no legal weight, with 257 voting for independence, 16 against, and one spoilt ballot. “There’s an issue with the sheer volume of people expected to be accommodated,” the chairwoman of the Barnham residents’ association, Helen Beck, told AFP earlier. “Barnham is a small village. There will be nothing for the (lodged) people to do, nowhere to go.” Under plans by Britain’s government, the base near the village in rural eastern England will be used to accommodate 931 migrants. The village has a population of 584. Residents were asked whether they supported seeking a “crown dependency status” similar to that of Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man. Parish council chair John Bauer said this would allow the village to “retain loyalty to the crown” while removing itself from Home Office jurisdiction. – Safety concern – Residents in both Barnham and Piddington say they are also worried about locals’ safety, particularly that of women. “We’ve been told they (the asylum seekers) are all males. We don’t know where they are from, their background,” Beck said. “People are anxious about walking alone, walking their dog in darkness if an additional 900 men arrive in the area,” she said. In the Piddington vote in September, 285 out of 312 votes were cast in favour of “pursuing self-determination”. The government plans to house around 1,250 asylum seekers on a former defence ministry site close to Piddington village, all single men between 18 and 65. Britain’s centre-left government, in power since July 2024, has vowed to end the use of hotels as migrant accommodation following a public outcry. It plans to move all those currently in hotels — a policy inherited from the last Conservative government — to former military bases by 2029. But Beck said that there were questions about whether military-style accommodation was suitable for people “fleeing a conflict or persecution”, adding that it was also “significantly more expensive than hotels”. entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? entertainment.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. Nigerian citizens enjoy visa-free entry for short stays of up to 60 days without needing a paid eTA, leaving more room in your budget for safaris and coastal stays. Rwanda Not everyone wants their year-end holiday to feel like a non-stop sprint, and Rwanda is built for travellers who prefer scenery, clean air, and an unhurried pace. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. entertainment.title: Visa Report Identifies Opportunity to Integrate Digital Payments with SMEs Business Operations in Nigeria
entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. entertainment.description: Tems receiving the Best African Music Performance at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Northwestern loses in heartbreaking fashion as it falls to Minnesota 20-17. In a game that looked poised to go to overtime after the ‘Cats scored with just 27 seconds remaining in the game, Minnesota gave payback for last year’s Wrigley Field matchup by kicking a walk-off field goal to win the game. Nicco Marchiol had a solid day and performed well in the eye test, but there were a plethora of incompletions that could have altered the result of the game. Griffin Wilde also had a solid game, catching five passes for 77 yards and a touchdown. Luke Dehnicke showed his emerging talent as a tight end, catching three passes for 66 yards. This game marks the first four-game losing streak in the David Braun era at Northwestern. The Gophers kicked it away for a touchback to open the penultimate regular-season game. The ‘Cats’ offense started things off with runs to Komolafe and Drew Wagner, picking up the first down to move the chains. Komolafe then broke off a 14-yard run to keep things going, but Minnesota’s defense forced an incompletion and short run to bring up third down. Another Marchiol incompletion to Wilde brought out Northwestern’s punt unit, and the Gophers’ first possession started at their own 20. Minnesota QB Drake Lindsey started out in the air with completions to his tight end Roman Voss and running back Darius Taylor to bring up a third-and-4. The ‘Cats stood strong, and Jamaal Johnson got home for a sack to force the punt. The three-and-out gave NU the ball right back at the 43-yard line. On offense, a second-down jet sweep to Drew Wagner squeaked the ‘Cats past the first-down marker, but then Marchiol and Wilde failed to connect yet again to put NU behind schedule. A fake handoff led to Marchiol being drilled behind the line of scrimmage, setting up a third-and-15 where Sawchuk’s run barely got back to the initial line of scrimmage. After two short gains, Northwestern surged into the backfield on third-and-short, but Minnesota’s TJ Thomas’ second effort kept the drive alive. Thomas then picked up 18 yards on a short completion as the Gopher offense found a rhythm and moved to the Northwestern 42. However, a holding call a couple of plays later led to Minnesota stalling out and setting up a 48-yard field goal try. The Gophers’ kicker pulled the ball left, and the game remained scoreless.

sports.title: Ravens’ 2026 season has come to a crashing halt
sports.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Trainers attend to Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens kneels after getting hurt on the first play of the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images It took just one play. As optimistically as it began, the 2026 Ravens season is all but finished. On the first day of November, on his first snap back from a high-ankle sprain, Lamar Jackson injured his right thumb when his throwing hand struck the wrist of Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau. Jackson knew something was wrong immediately, sprinting straight to the sideline and then to the locker room. The two-time MVP has since had surgery on his thumb with a late-season return technically in play – if it even matters. At this point, Jackson is the Baltimore Ravens, and his contract reflects that. Many want to bash the supporting cast, the coaches and the front office, but it just isn’t realistic for a team paying a star quarterback that much to also have stars at every other position. What did the Chiefs look like without Patrick Mahomes last year? What did the Bengals look like without Joe Burrow? What would the Bills look like without Josh Allen? On top of losing Jackson, the Ravens have suffered a rash of injuries elsewhere, primarily on the offensive line. A position group that typically thrives on continuity is operating with a new offensive coordinator, a new offensive line coach, and a rotating door of new starters. This year, the unit has had five different centers and four different right guards. Has the offensive line been good enough? No. But we never got to see the vision. Heck, we never even got to see Jackson and Zay Flowers play a full game together. The full extent of the Ravens’ woes came to a head five days after the Jacksonville Jaguars. With undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano making his first start, the Ravens were once again trounced at home, this time in a downpour. We all expected the offense to struggle, and predictably, it did. But once again, the defense let the dam break. Is that partly a product of the offense’s struggles? Probably. Still, it looked more like a group of unmotivated, aging players struggling to adjust to a new defensive system. Marlon Humphrey and Malaki Starks were both burned for big plays, and the middle of the field — an area that has plagued this defense for years — was wide open all night for Trevor Lawrence. But tucked in among those move was an underrated one: the Browns brought in a favorite of new defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg by signing former Jets linebacker Quincy Williams, whose style of play on the field is as dynamic as his mouth can be during interviews. Fair play to them for that but we expect more from ourselves.” Davies also provided an update on Jhon Solis, who missed the game after picking up a knock while on international duty. “Jhon picked up a knock on international duty that we thought he would run off,” he said. “But he wasn’t able to do that. “My understanding is that it’s not a long-term thing but it was investigated more today so we should know tomorrow.” Asked whether Solis could be available on Wednesday, Davies added: “I think there is a chance but I don’t know how big that chance is right now based on what I was told yesterday.”

sports.title: Fans with Saturday tickets to RSM Classic are out of luck, no gallery for final round Monday
sports.description: Heavy rain led to poor course conditions at Sea Island Resort's Seaside Course in St. Simon's Island, Georgia, forcing the PGA Tour to postpone Saturday's third round of the 2026 RSM Classic to Sunday and push the final round back to Monday. So what about fans who had tickets to see Saturday's action in-person? Tough luck. "Only Sunday tickets will be accepted tomorrow," the tournament wrote in an Instagram post . "Due to our refund and exchange policy, we will not honor Saturday tickets tomorrow." sports.title: Grading Purdue football: Questionable QB decision and Fs all-around in blowout loss to Wisconsin
sports.description: WEST LAFAYETTE − Purdue football 's nose dive continues. The Boilermakers had the ball just 49 seconds before they trailed 14-0. Wisconsin (7-4) had the opening it needed on its way to a 42-10 victory . The Badgers sent Purdue (3-8) fans exiting the season's final home game with a fifth straight loss, and now with 19 consecutive losses in the series. A questionable starting quarterback decision backfired and Purdue's wet paper bag defense again provided a big day for a struggling offense. In a season marred by failures, you can imagine how the report card looks from Purdue's loss to Wisconsin at Ross-Ade Stadium. OFFENSE GRADE: F The offensive line was supposed to be an upgrade this year, but it's becoming hard to find evidence supporting that claim. Not a lot of analysis needs to go into this grade. Statistics are all you need. Purdue averaged 3.6 yards per play and totaled 199 yards. DEFENSE GRADE: F By halftime, the Badgers already had accumulated 52 more rushing yards (185) than their season average (133). Purdue's defense is beyond repair. Wisconsin quarterback Colton Joseph didn't start the last two games but returned behind center after Ryan Hopkins was injured late in a Nov. 14 game against Maryland. Joseph then became the latest QB to torch the Big Ten's worst defense. The Badgers totaled 508 yards, 381 of those on the ground. Wisconsin was 13-for-17 on converting third and fourth downs. SPECIAL TEAMS GRADE: B Jacobo Echeverria Lozano attempted, and made, a career-long 53-yard field goal in the second quarter. It pads his case for the Lou Groza Award, which is bolstered because Purdue's offense is good, but not good enough to get into the end zone in a lot of cases. Still, the freshman has taken advantage. Dylan Drennan also has been a weapon, though Purdue doesn't have a competent enough defense to fully benefit from Drennan's leg. The risk returning kickoffs has not paid off. Best bet for Purdue is to take the touchback, or fair catch if the kickoff doesn't reach the end zone. COACHING GRADE: F You can't give me a valid reason why quarterback Evans Chuba started this game over Ryan Browne. No package or perceived advantage makes sense. It's even more indefensible after seeing the results of that decision. Chuba threw two incompletions during a three-and-out. Browne led Purdue on consecutive scoring drives after entering. Purdue had a second week to tinker with the defense since Kevin Kane's firing , and somehow looked better on the road against a ranked Iowa team with little time to adapt to the staff change. Waiting until you're down 18 points to uncover the trick play portion of the playbook seems like off timing. GAME MVP If Ryan Hopkins is healthy, Colton Joseph probably doesn't even start this game. Instead, Joseph's return as the Badgers starting quarterback. He rushed for 187 yards and 2 touchdowns, passed for 114 yards and also hauled in a 13-yard touchdown reception. sports.description: MLS star Thomas Muller explains how promotion and relegation changes league dynamic originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Now 37 years old, Thomas Muller has greatly enjoyed his time in Major League Soccer. After leaving Bayern Munich in the summer of 2025 following a glittering 17-year career with the Bavarian giants, Muller joined the Vancouver Whitecaps and has brought his winning mentality along. Muller reached the MLS Cup final in his first half-season, losing to Lionel Messi and Inter Miami at the final hurdle. This season, Vancouver won the Western Conference regular season title, and are set to be the No. 1 seed on their side of the bracket in the playoffs. Always his enlightening, outspoken self, Muller took the time to explain how MLS is different without promotion and relegation, from a player's perspective. He believes there are real, on-field consequences to having a closed pyramid, ones which players can notice by the style of play across the league. MORE: Explaining the Jamal Musiala contract dispute which has Bayern Munich receiving criticism Thomas Muller explains how MLS is different without relegation Thomas Muller was asked how he feels Major League Soccer handles being a closed, single-entity league without promotion and relegation. The 37-year-old stopped short of criticizing the league for not having promotion and relegation, but he did explain the differences between having open movement throughout the pyramid and having a closed system without the threat of relegation at the bottom of the table. As Muller explains, there is a pressure for those under relegation threat that changes the way some teams play. Without that threat, as there is in MLS, teams play more openly — more risky, as Muller insinuates — which can increase the range of possible performances. It can cause players to make excellent plays, but also commit grave errors you wouldn't see in a less-risky playing style at a team battling relegation. "There is no relegation," Muller explained at the end of the 2026 regular season. "There is no big pressure. There is 'oh yea, we do a rebuild.' Nobody's happy to lose, but it's totally different when you fight for getting relegated. Maybe you lose, but for the whole year, the whole club, you lose people working at the club and the budget changes. It's totally different for fans, the pressure. The players maybe have no contract for next year when you go down. "So the playing style changes. When you play a bottom-of-the-league team in Europe, they fight for their lives. That’s not just from an individual perspective, though Simmons has been great in that regard, posting three tackles for loss, two sacks, and two passes defended in his two weeks with the Bears. The unit as a whole has benefited from the increased double teams the All-Pro tackle has faced, allowing just 4.5 yards per play when he’s been on the field and ranking in the top 10 in EPA/play and success rate allowed since Simmons got here. But there’s one aspect in which, while improved, the Bears have remained somewhat middling at: defending the run. That’s why NFL.com ‘s Brooke Cersosimo forecasts New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne might be a problem for Chicago on Sunday. “Etienne returned to action last week after missing five games with a hamstring injury and looked rusty — to say the least — rushing for 14 yards on eight carries. technology.title: AWS got hit by an outage too. Here's why you didn't hear about it
technology.description: My editor asked me this week "why is everything except AWS breaking?" It's a great question! They haven't been in the headlines! In fact, as they are wont to do, AWS spokesperson Patrick Neighorn g ot salty to a reporter about how unreliable Downdetector is when it started showing them as impacted. If you'll permit me a small digression, this stems from a misunderstanding of what Downdetector is for. Historically the AWS status site was so hilariously slow to reflect the lived customer experience that some jackass (me) built a rewriter that sits at stop.lying.cloud to make it a smidgen more realistic. As a result, the question people are really trying to answer when they visit Downdetector is "my app just broke; is it my crappy code or is there a global event going on?" There are mitigations for both, but they look nothing alike. AWS view crowdsourced reports of the form "the internet is broken, must be AWS" as a stain upon their honor. In fact, it's a badge of their own success, as "the internet" and "AWS" have become inextricably linked in people's minds. But back to my editor's question, "why didn't AWS go down?" Easy: it did. Everything breaks, all the time, including the narrative AWS now has 34 generally available commercial regions, of which two are currently smoking craters due to the Iran conflict. Each of these has hundreds of services that AWS offers to customers, of which a dozen or so are high quality, if I'm being characteristically uncharitable. They experience degradation in various ways, and they go largely unnoticed. But on November 15, AWS confirmed an incident that disrupted 11 of those ~12 good services in their oldest and most important region, us-east-1. At 3:05 AM PST, they stated that they started seeing sign-up errors, authentication issues, and connectivity issues. Five minutes later engineers were engaged. Not to be outdone, their status page swung into action after a leisurely coffee, and posted its first indication of an incident 93 minutes later. (See previous comments on stop.lying.cloud ). The all-clear showed up at 6:53 AM. Every site has downtime. Sometimes it blows up publicly, other times nobody seems to notice. Heck, AWS said in September that it had experienced permanent data loss in its two smoking craters, but after that news cycle passed I haven't heard a thing about it. I do think it's patently unreasonable to blame them for this specific problem; "acts of war" are kinda hard to predict from the corporate planning meeting. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

science.title: 'Star Trek: First Contact' at 30: Resistance is futile when it comes to the 'Next Generation' crew's greatest big-screen adventure
science.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. But following some impassioned talk about making the Borg "pay for what they've done", he's finally talked down from his rage by 21st-century stowaway Lily Sloane (Alfre Woodard). She points out that his Moby-Dick-esque obsession is on the verge of going full Ahab, and he eventually sees sense, issuing the order to abandon the Enterprise and destroy the hive. It's a masterclass showcasing the ever-brilliant Stewart's impressive range, as the out-of-control captain's rarely seen temper reaches fever pitch, before normal service is resumed. His subsequent apology to Worf — "As a matter of fact, I think you're the bravest man I've ever known" — is simply perfect. And just as the franchise's zenith, "The Wrath of Khan", is built around Kirk and Khan's decades-old feud, "First Contact" is precision engineered to get the most out of Jean-Luc. This was the right "Star Trek" at the right time, a film that put "TNG"'s greatest villains on a collision course with the origins of Starfleet. science.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) And SpaceX is very serious about Starship reuse. Musk has said that the company wants to launch about 10,000 Starship missions per year by 2030. This mind-boggling cadence will help the company build out two enormous megaconstellations in low Earth orbit — the next iteration of its Starlink broadband network, which will consist of about 100,000 satellites , and its Starmind AI data-center constellation, which will be 10 times bigger than that .
